verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Jodhpur stone processors with own quarry linkage or verified domestic order books; avoid kiln-dependent and export-concentrated units until local demand and raw-material supply stabilise.
title: Jodhpur stone, granite & marble processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Jodhpur stone unit buys rough blocks or limestone, cuts and polishes them into slabs and tiles, and sells into construction and export markets.** Cash is tied in block inventory and finished slabs before dispatch; value sits in polishing quality and block yield, not in the yard. Rajasthan's granite and marble cluster benefits from proximity to raw material sources, with group-owned quarries meeting around 40% of raw material needs in one rated case [11]. The state backdrop is weak: Rajasthan GST collections are -4.7% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand is +4.0% against India +9.5% [D]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the unit depends on kiln-fed limestone; if yes, ask for the import plan and its funding, because input cost is the swing factor.**

## Where the growth is
**National stone output is still expanding: IIP NIC 23 is +11.4% YoY and +10.2% Apr-to-date [D], so demand exists even as Jodhpur's local signals lag.** Peer results are mixed: Midwest revenue rose 35% YoY in 1QFY27 [5] and 9MFY26 revenue was ₹429.81 crore with EBITDA of ₹116.05 crore [7], while Aro's June 2026 quarter net sales fell 23.72% YoY to ₹20.62 crore [6]. **Pursue processors with domestic order books, own-quarry linkage and polishing capacity already running; avoid pure kiln-dependent units and exporters concentrated in one foreign region, as the European concentration risk in one rated group shows [9].**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the yard.** Take monthly stock and sales statements, and a monthly block-purchase register reconciled to permits, given the 18-versus-32-tonne loading issue [2]. **Ask for monthly GST returns and electricity bills; if GST turnover falls below the sanctioned drawing power for two months, cut limits.** Peer working-capital utilisation of around 56% of sanctioned limits [8] is a useful benchmark for sizing. Keep tenors short and take a second charge on quarry or land where available. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch input substitution and dispatch weight.** If a borrower starts importing limestone without a funded plan [1], or dispatch weights drift from permit weights [2], treat it as a cash-flow warning.

## Sources and gaps
**Local sources say little about Jodhpur's own processing volumes, so this note leans on first principles and peer results.** Collect from customer: city-level processing capacity, average realisations per square metre, and debtor days. The data pack is cited as [D].

## The call
**Caution, not avoidance: the national output trend supports lending, but Rajasthan's GST and power signals plus the limestone shortage cap the appetite.** Lend to quarry-linked, domestically sold processors; decline kiln-dependent and single-market exporters.
